figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 1
figures_and_tables_checked.review_basis: Supplied full text, caption, and page-image review notes.
figures_and_tables_checked.findings: Training/inference schematic. Training incorporates encoded rendered observations; inference follows an internal imagined sequence. Conceptual clinician/robot artwork is not evidence of human or hardware experiments. One sequential path is drawn, not demonstrated branching over candidate actions.
figures_and_tables_checked.limits: Initial encoded inference image versus §2.4 initialization remains ambiguous; no quantitative transition or timing evidence is supplied by the schematic.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 2
figures_and_tables_checked.review_basis: Supplied full text, caption, and page-image review notes.
figures_and_tables_checked.findings: Synthetic noisy expert trajectory, renderer, encoders, Gaussian prior/posterior, recurrent belief, decoder/reward/policy branches, and KL/reconstruction/reward/pose losses.
figures_and_tables_checked.limits: Diagrammatic reward/decoder notation is not proof of shared weights. No numerical noise scales or model dimensions are supplied. Goal exclusion applies to dynamics, not to all heads.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Table 1
figures_and_tables_checked.review_basis: Supplied table text and structured page-image review notes; units cross-checked on page 7.
figures_and_tables_checked.findings: All reported rows for CUReg, EUReg, FVRNet, and DreamReg retained separately for CAMUS and µ-RegPro. Main-model results also represented as qualified metric_results.
figures_and_tables_checked.limits: Direct image-cell verification outstanding. Standard-deviation sampling unit and run count unspecified. FPS is not accompanied by dispersion or a full timing protocol.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Figure 3
figures_and_tables_checked.review_basis: Supplied caption and page-image review notes.
figures_and_tables_checked.findings: Four selected qualitative examples: two CAMUS and two µ-RegPro rows, comparing initial alignment, three baselines, DreamReg, and ground truth, with red intensity-difference displays.
figures_and_tables_checked.limits: No per-example metric values, selection protocol, scale bars, error colorbar, or independent patient count. Qualitative residual reduction is not a clinical plausibility study.

figures_and_tables_checked.label: Table 2
figures_and_tables_checked.review_basis: Supplied table text and structured page-image review notes.
figures_and_tables_checked.findings: Full CAMUS ablation rows retained. Full method has the best reported mean in each column; ablated variants have mixed relative rankings.
figures_and_tables_checked.limits: Pose-only is not uniformly worst. Exact retained architecture/losses and statistical repetition protocol remain unclear.

scope_choices: This is automated API model review and skeptical second-pass synthesis of supplied full text and prior model-generated page/image notes, not independent human verification, code execution, or replication.

All 11 supplied text pages and all 11 page-level visual-review notes were read. Actual PDF page images were not directly available to this response, so direct visual inspection cannot honestly be certified.
Source path, page count, and SHA-256 are supplied registry metadata, not newly verified filesystem facts. No files, repository, external articles, supplements, or dataset records were accessed.
No JSON Schema validator, graph assembler, regression tests, file writes, or independent source-hash checks were executed.
The modeled coordinate is acquisition pose/internal registration refinement. Five or seven rollout steps are not five or seven clinical time points or a validated clinical-time horizon.

Training trajectories are synthetic noisy interpolations between initial and ground-truth poses. Introductory wording about monitored probe maneuvers does not establish clinician-recorded trajectories.

Inference uses a fixed input volume and target slice, with prior-only latent feedback. No new measured slices, live observation assimilation, physical probe motion, or clinical closed-loop control is demonstrated.
Figure 1 appears to show an initial encoded inference image, whereas §2.4 specifies fixed volume/goal embeddings and zero initial pose/belief. Exact initial-image handling needs clarification.
The recurrent/stochastic latent model is implemented, but no direct prior-transition prediction, prior-only generated-slice fidelity, or horizon-dependent rollout-error evaluation is reported.

The L4 assignment concerns a supervised model-coupled computational registration policy. It does not establish actor–critic learning, imagined-return optimization, explicit candidate search, a separate L3 experiment, or therapeutic control.
The Gaussian latent does not establish calibrated transformation uncertainty, aleatoric/epistemic decomposition, trajectory coverage, uncertainty-based abstention, or risk-sensitive planning.

The narrow R2 facet uses held-out source-reported clinical prostate imaging with a case-level split, not synthetic trajectory holdouts. It does not establish validation on actual probe-action sequences or independently acquired live 2D targets.

CAMUS is reported as 1000 cardiac US volumes, while its cited reference concerns 2D echocardiography. The 3D construction, volume/case/patient mapping, and exact official-split counts are insufficiently explained. Reported quantities are preserved rather than corrected from background knowledge.
For µ-RegPro, 73 volumes, a 7:1:2 case split, and 120 test slices are reported; exact integer case counts and patient-level independence are not supplied or computed.
Clinical eligibility, demographics, acquisition sites, scanner vendors, dataset versions, access terms, consent/IRB, and privacy controls are not sufficiently reported.

Separate training/evaluation on two datasets does not establish external validation of a frozen model. No subgroup, site, corruption, missing-modality, deformation, or action-distribution shift analysis is reported.

Evaluation targets are slices resampled from volumes and do not model real tissue deformation. Acoustic fidelity, contact pressure, ultrasound artifacts under physical probe motion, and deformable-world generalization remain unvalidated.
The renderer is called physics-based, but the supplied description primarily specifies slice sampling; an acoustic forward model or validated tissue-contact mechanism is not established.

Pose frames, rotation parameterization, additive transform semantics, normalization, voxel spacing, interpolation details, noise scales, zero-norm cosine handling, and exact update indexing are insufficiently specified.
Latent dimensions, model size, pretrained assets, complete learning-rate schedule, training time, run seeds, and full reproducibility configuration are not reported.
Accuracy values are reported as mean±standard deviation, but the standard-deviation unit, number of runs, within-patient dependence, confidence intervals, and significance tests are not reported.
Main and ablation table values were transcribed using supplied text plus supplied structured visual notes. Direct image-based rechecking remains outstanding.

The full model has the best reported six-metric means, but pose-only is not uniformly worst among ablations. Ablations do not separately isolate recurrence, stochasticity, action conditioning, shortcut prevention, prior fidelity, or the complete meaning of the pose-only configuration.

The reported 40 and 56 FPS do not validate workflow-level latency or clinical acceptability. Timing batch size, preprocessing inclusion, synchronization, dispersion, and load are not reported; EUReg is faster in Table 1.

No empirically justified effective horizon, registration-success tolerance, clinical safety threshold, exploitation test, action-support audit, operational guard, abstention, escalation, security test, monitoring plan, or authorization is reported.
No actual human reader study, prospective shadow use, patient feasibility intervention, comparative clinical utility, or authorized monitored deployment is established.
The printed project URL establishes only that a URL is supplied; working code, weights, license, prompts, and independent reproduction are not established.

Cited Dreamer, DayDreamer, Medical World Model, clinical ultrasound, and robotics studies were inspected only as bibliography/background within this paper; their capabilities and readiness were not transferred to DreamReg.

Some supplied chunk-level review notes say other page ranges were unavailable. Those statements describe earlier partial review packets and are superseded for text coverage by the complete pages 1–11 supplied here.
